findings.title: Loop leaks modal state into the command assertions that follow
findings.message: After the page/modal loop, `d.modal` is left as `true` from the final iteration (`modal=true`, page=`"suite"`). The subsequent `d.commands()` call and `r.Invoke(...)` assertions therefore run with modal state still enabled. If the command registry or the demo view behavior is modal-dependent (which is likely given the test explicitly iterates modal states), the command assertions are implicitly coupled to leftover loop state rather than a clean baseline, making the test fragile and its intent unclear.
findings.suggestion: Explicitly reset the demo state to a known baseline after the validation loop, e.g. `d.tab = "overview"; d.modal = false`, before calling `d.commands()`, so the command assertions are independent of loop leftovers.

findings.title: Missing blank line between function declarations
findings.message: The file body ends with `}` on line 62 and `func TestServicePayloadContracts` starts on line 63 with no blank line between the two top-level declarations. This is unusual formatting for Go test files (gofmt will not insert it, but virtually every codebase and editor convention separates top-level declarations with a blank line), and it makes the file harder to scan.
findings.suggestion: Add a blank line between the closing brace of `TestAllPagesAndModalContracts` and the `func TestServicePayloadContracts` declaration.

findings.title: Replay run failure discards the captured output
findings.message: When the replay binary fails (or is killed by ctx cancellation), only the exec error (e.g. "exit status 1") is returned and the captured stdout/stderr in `out` is discarded. This demo exists to surface results to the user via d.service, so a bare exit-status error gives no diagnostic clue about why the replay failed (common when the `replay` binary was never built).
findings.suggestion: Wrap the error and include the combined output so the demo shows what the replay binary printed, e.g. `return "", fmt.Errorf("replay run failed: %w: %s", err, out)` (add `fmt` to the imports).
